risk_if_not_implemented: Without Product Tampering and Counterfeiting (PTC), counterfeit, non-conforming or compromised components and services may enter the environment through the supply chain. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Modification / Loss of System Integrity (R-AM-2), Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Component Impact (R-SC-7), Loss of Authenticity / Provenance (R-IP-5), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Fraud, Corruption and/or Intentional Criminal Conduct (MT-14), Counterfeit / Non-Conforming Products (MT-20), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Third-Party Incident Response & Recovery Capabilities
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure response/recovery planning and testing are conducted with critical suppliers/providers.
compensating_control_1.justification: Third-Party Incident Response & Recovery Capabilities (TPM-21) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Product Tampering and Counterfeiting (PTC) (TDA-09) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) Plan
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to develop a plan for Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) associated with the development, acquisition, maintenance and disposal of Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS), including documenting selected mitigating actions and monitoring performance against those plans.
compensating_control_2.justification: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) Plan (RSK-20) provides risk identification and prioritization that compensates for the absence of Product Tampering and Counterfeiting (PTC) (TDA-09) by enabling informed decisions about where to focus resources to manage residual exposure. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
